prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of glucagon-like peptide-1 and the identification of its active form that enabled incretin-based therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: I keep B013 alone, with Drucker, Holst and Mojsov. The round-1 exchange confirmed that the dispute is not about the science: all six of us accept a complete, independently confirmed chain from proglucagon processing and the insulinotropic action of GLP-1(7-36), through receptor biology and the gut-pancreas axis, to long-acting agonists with cardiovascular, renal and weight outcome data. The only real question is what the citation honours. I think a Physiology or Medicine prize is best anchored on the discovery side, where the new understanding was created (native hormone physiology, peptide identity and synthesis of the active form, receptor and gut-pancreas biology), while the citation text can state the therapeutic consequence openly. That principle, applied consistently, gives this trio. A single-achievement prize also avoids cutting B013 below three names to make room for a second part.
statement.case_against: The strongest objection, which I do not dismiss, is that this trio leaves out Knudsen, whose acylated analogues turned a peptide with a half-life of minutes into liraglutide and semaglutide, and that a prize that stops at discovery can look detached from the therapy that changed practice. Mojsov's early-1980s priority over the active peptide is contested and I still cannot verify it from the supplied record, so my choice rests on the weight of the contribution as described and not on a settled priority finding. Habener sits outside the supplied credit and cannot be weighed here. A discovery-only trio also draws a line between academic and industrial work that is not always sharp.

responses.point: Perlmann holds Drucker, Holst and Knudsen and argues that the step that made the hormone a medicine, the long-acting analogue, rests more clearly on Knudsen than Mojsov's contested peptide priority does.
responses.response: This is the strongest form of the other trio, and his point about DPP-4 degradation and half-life shows that the analogues were an enabling step and not mere optimisation. I still do not move, for two reasons. First, uncertainty about Mojsov's priority argues for stating the exclusion openly, not for choosing the name that is easier to verify. Second, if the citation honours translation, the same reasoning invites other industrial contributors and the prize loses its discovery anchor. I accept that this is a judgement about what the prize is for. I also note that his own stated confidence is lower on that point than on the field, and that we agree on the principle-first framing.

responses.point: Wahren-Herlenius keeps a physiology-plus-translation citation because the prize would be hollow without the step that turned the peptide into a therapy, and says she could support Drucker, Holst and Mojsov if the committee wants a discovery-only prize.
responses.response: I take her last sentence as the useful common ground: if the committee settles on discovery as the criterion, the trio is Drucker, Holst and Mojsov, and she can accept it. I disagree that the prize would be hollow, because the citation I propose names the therapies as the consequence of the discovery, so the medical significance is stated without crediting the engineering. I agree with her restriction of the scope to diabetes, obesity and the cardiovascular and renal outcome evidence, and I have kept neurological and other emerging indications out of the wording.

responses.point: El-Manira argues that Mojsov's identification and synthesis of the active peptide is the missing step between Holst's physiology and any drug, and that dropping her would remove the only peptide-level contribution from the trio.
responses.response: I agree with that structural argument and it is the main reason I keep her. I also note his caveat that the priority needs careful documentation and that a Knudsen version is a legitimate alternative if her claim proves unsafe. I share that conditional: if the record supplied to the committee showed her claim to be unsound, I would move to Knudsen and not leave the seat empty. Nothing in the first round supplied such evidence, so the contested priority is a reason for care in the citation wording, which credits the identification of the active form without asserting priority over others.

responses.point: The chair frames B042 or B008 as easier to attribute than B013 if the committee cannot agree on a defensible three, even though he rates their overall impact lower.
responses.response: I agree that attribution is the real risk for B013 and that B042 and B008 are the fallbacks, which is why they are my two alternatives. I do not think the committee is yet at the point of abandoning B013, because the disagreement is confined to one seat and to a stated principle. B008 has a cleaner two-person credit than B042, which still has the Eshhar gap and a Rosenberg role best described as adoptive transfer in general, but its overall impact is smaller. I would use either only as an alternative and not as a second part alongside B013, since a second part would force a cut among Drucker, Holst and Mojsov.

responses.point: Sandberg would not recommend combining B013 with B042 in one prize because the three-person cap would force Drucker, Holst and Mojsov to be reduced, and would prefer HPV vaccines as fallback if Eshhar is judged fatal to CAR-T.
responses.response: I agree that no second part is worth reducing the B013 trio. On the fallback, I still rank B008 above B010 in my alternatives because the antisense credit is two names and cleaner than the HPV trio, where Zhou is deceased and the parallel VLP groups leave priority unverified. I take his point that HPV has stronger population-level evidence than anything on the B008 side, and I would revisit that order if the committee showed the three HPV names to be cleanly separable. I do not regard his earlier co-authorship with me as shared judgement, and my positions here are independent of it.

uncertainties: Whether Mojsov's early-1980s priority holds up against the Habener group record, which is outside the supplied names; I could not verify it, and I would move to Knudsen if it were shown not to hold.
Whether the committee settles on discovery alone or on discovery plus drug design, which determines the third seat more than any scientific fact.
Long-term safety and outcome data for obesity indications are still accumulating, and the citation should stay within established diabetes, obesity, cardiovascular and renal indications.
Whether B042 can be defended with Eshhar outside the credited names, and whether B008's two-name credit is as clean as it appears, if a fallback is needed.
statement.conflict_note: Updated disclosure: I have still not checked co-authorship between myself and any credited name on a shortlisted ballot, and my spatial transcriptomics (Science 2016), single-cell and brain-atlas work does not involve the GLP-1, CAR-T or antisense candidates. Sandberg disclosed co-authorship with me, which the OpenAlex record in my profile also lists, and neither of us is a credited name. I see no conflict requiring recusal on B013 or the alternatives, and I would recuse if a credited name proved to be a close collaborator.
